context:
Treat `benchbox.core.publishing` as a prototype inventory, not as the architecture to preserve verbatim.
Start by mapping its genuinely useful concepts (artifact metadata, publish targets, retention intent)
against the real product surface in `benchbox.core.results.exporter`, `benchbox/cli/output.py`,
`benchbox/cli/commands/export.py`, `benchbox/cli/commands/results.py`, and the run export path in
`benchbox/cli/commands/run.py`.

The first supported contract should publish already-exported result bundles, because that reuses the
canonical schema-v2 artifacts BenchBox already writes and avoids another serialization pathway. Build
persistent publication metadata around those bundles, then layer optional post-run publishing on top.

Keep backend behavior honest: only generate public/shareable URLs when the configured backend can
actually provide them. For local or private targets, expose durable references and metadata rather
than pretending a short code is a usable permalink. Once the supported flow exists, collapse or
delete the leftover prototype-only branches so the repo does not carry two parallel systems.
description:
The completed item `_project/DONE/infrastructure-publishing/planning/automated-data-publishing-pipeline.yaml`
intended to add a supported workflow for publishing benchmark results to local/cloud storage,
generating permalinks, and managing published artifacts. The implementation delivered a substantial
prototype under `benchbox/core/publishing/` plus a strong self-contained test suite, but it stopped
short of becoming a BenchBox feature.

This TODO is now explicitly scoped as the BenchBox-local artifact publication track. It should own
`benchbox publish` style workflows for copying canonical result bundles to local/cloud storage and
tracking durable publication metadata. Hosted result submission (`benchbox submit`) and the public
explorer at `benchbox.dev/results/` are tracked by the companion results-platform TODO cluster
created from `_project/analysis/benchbox-results-platform-strategy.md`.

Current state after review:
- The publishing module has zero runtime or CLI consumers outside its own tests.
- BenchBox already has a canonical result path in `benchbox.core.results.exporter` that powers
  `benchbox run`, `benchbox export`, and `benchbox results`; the publishing module duplicates
  serialization and output concerns instead of extending that path.
- Publication state is process-local and in-memory (`ArtifactManager`, `PermalinkRegistry`), so
  published artifacts, share links, and retention bookkeeping do not survive process exit.
- Several advertised capabilities are incomplete or misleading: `secondary_storage` is unused,
  notifications are placeholders, and `PublishFormat.PARQUET` is declared but not actually emitted.
- The module generates short links, but BenchBox ships no resolver service, URL policy, or documented
  public-link contract that makes those links broadly useful.

This follow-up effort treats the original work as a prototype that should either be promoted into
a supported user workflow or remain prunable dead code. The implementation plan below assumes the
feature is worth keeping and focuses on making it genuinely useful by integrating it with the
canonical results/export/history path rather than preserving a parallel subsystem.

anti_patterns.dont: build a second result serialization pipeline
anti_patterns.instead: publish the real exported bundle instead
anti_patterns.why: BenchBox already has a canonical schema-v2 exporter and companion file model

anti_patterns.dont: emit fake permalinks with no resolver or addressability contract
anti_patterns.why: users will treat them as durable links

anti_patterns.dont: expose publishing only as hidden plumbing with zero CLI/API consumers
anti_patterns.instead: land a supported user-facing workflow early
anti_patterns.why: that reproduces the original prototype failure

anti_patterns.dont: keep publication registries in memory only
anti_patterns.why: publish/list/retention/share workflows must survive process exit

anti_patterns.dont: preserve unused prototype promises like secondary mirrors or notifications without a real integration path
anti_patterns.instead: defer them until the core flow works
anti_patterns.why: they inflate scope and maintenance burden

work_units.notes:
Capture the original intent (`automated-data-publishing-pipeline`, commit `97138d3a5`) versus the
current execution reality. The matrix should explicitly classify each prototype capability as:
keep and integrate, redesign, or drop. Include concrete evidence for zero-consumer status and for
overlap with `benchbox.core.results.exporter`.
work_units.summary: Write a gap matrix comparing the prototype publishing module to the canonical results/export workflow

work_units.notes:
Add unit and integration coverage for the supported flow, then remove or collapse the leftover
prototype-only code paths that are no longer needed. If the feature still fails to earn real
product integration after this work, the repo should prefer pruning over carrying another dead
subsystem.
work_units.summary: Add end-to-end coverage and then retire or slim the remaining prototype-only surfaces

work_units.notes:
Decide the product shape before coding. At minimum, define whether BenchBox supports:
1) publishing an existing exported result bundle,
2) optional post-run publishing from `benchbox run`,
3) listing published artifacts/history,
4) retention/cleanup operations,
5) stable share links for local and/or cloud backends.
Hosted service submission is intentionally out of scope here; this item should recommend a local
or storage-backed `benchbox publish` surface and document why.
work_units.summary: Define the supported user workflows, CLI surface, and success criteria for publishing and sharing results

work_units.notes:
Replace the current process-local registry model with durable publication metadata. The store should
persist published artifact identity, source result bundle, storage targets, retention state, and
share-link metadata. The design should support local filesystem and cloud-path targets without
depending on an always-running service.
work_units.summary: Design and implement a persistent publication metadata model that survives process restart

work_units.notes:
The follow-up feature must publish the actual schema-v2 result bundle (`.json`, `.plans.json`,
`.tuning.json`) produced by `benchbox.core.results.exporter`, not a second JSON shape from
`Publisher._serialize_result()`. Unsupported prototype-only promises should either be implemented
through the canonical exporter or removed from the supported surface.
work_units.summary: Refactor publishing to reuse canonical result bundles instead of duplicating result serialization

work_units.notes:
Add the supported user entry point for publishing and inspecting published artifacts. The workflow
should work on already-exported result files first, because that is the smallest broadly useful
contract and naturally composes with `benchbox run`, `benchbox export`, and future automation.
work_units.summary: Implement a first-class CLI/API path for publishing existing result bundles

work_units.notes:
Once publishing an existing bundle is supported, wire an optional publish step into the canonical
run lifecycle. The hook must reuse the already-exported bundle and preserve quiet-mode/output rules.
Avoid special-case behavior that bypasses the exporter or creates different artifacts depending on
whether publishing is enabled.
work_units.summary: Add an optional post-run publish hook that composes with the existing run/export lifecycle

work_units.notes:
A short code or URL is only useful when it resolves to something durable. Define how BenchBox will
represent published locations for:
- local filesystem targets,
- directly addressable object storage roots,
- non-public/private cloud locations.
If BenchBox cannot resolve a public URL for a backend, expose a truthful reference (storage URI or
metadata record) instead of a fake permalink.
work_units.summary: Implement backend-specific addressability rules so share links are real, stable, and documented

work_units.notes:
The current prototype can mark items archived in memory, but a supported feature needs durable
retention behavior, safe re-publication of existing bundles, and explicit idempotency rules for
duplicate content or duplicate publish requests.
work_units.summary: Add retention, republish, and idempotency semantics on top of the persistent publication store

work_units.notes:
Add CLI help, docs, and examples for both local and cloud publishing. The documentation must state
exactly what kind of link/reference a user gets for each backend and what persistence guarantees
BenchBox does and does not make.
work_units.summary: Document the workflow, configuration, and supported backends with user-facing examples
